Ruling

Full refund FULL_REFUND

Refund to the rider: SGD 4.50

The judge's explanation, as written

To both parties — the SGD 4.50 no-show fee is refunded to the rider in full, and no driver compensation is payable. The cancellation was made by the driver at 19:15:10 under reason code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE (EV-TRIP-02748). POL-NS-01 makes a no-show fee chargeable only if all four of its limbs hold, and limb (d) recognises only RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. The clause states in terms that DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE — the driver's own statement that he could not find the rider — does not satisfy limb (d). Limb (d) therefore fails, and the SGD 4.50 fee line on EV-FARE-02748 (payment status CHARGED, refund issued SGD 0.00) is not chargeable. The same clause then fixes the consequence by geography: where the driver's stationary fixes lie INSIDE the arrival radius this is a full refund of the cancellation fee with no driver compensation, and that is what the driver's own trace shows. POL-NS-03 does not apply, because that clause governs fixes outside the radius but within 400 m, and POL-NS-02's 'never arrived' branch would require fixes more than 400 m away. For the driver. What your record does establish is accepted, and it does not save the charge. You arrived at 19:11:48 (EV-TRIP-02748), inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the trace's first qualifying in-geofence fix is at the same second with a dwell start offset of 0.0 s. You held position for a continuous 200 seconds over 21 qualifying fixes, 19:11:48 to 19:15:08, against the 180-second free waiting period in force (platform_policy.free_wait_sec), so there is no POL-NS-06 shortfall (derived shortfall -20.0 s). The 'I'm Here' marker was not false under POL-NS-05: the trace placed you inside the radius at that second and you were stationary (nearest approach 0.44 m), not travelling at 15 km/h or more, so no false-arrival referral arises. The money is sound: the SGD 4.50 line reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd (4.50) and the schedule default, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. The trade-off the policy makes is that a correctly waited pickup recorded under the wrong reason code is still not chargeable; your own claim on this point does not press the fee and claims no POL-NS-07 payout, and it is right. For the rider. Independently of limb (d), POL-NS-04 exonerates you on all three limbs: you sent a locating message inside the waiting window ('at the lift lobby', 19:12:48, EV-CHAT-02748); the driver posted no reply within 120 seconds of it and made no in-app call before cancelling at 19:15:10; and your device stayed inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius on 40 of 40 fixes, maximum 19.67 m (EV-GPS-02748). Full refund, no driver compensation. Confidence is not reduced by POL-GEN-02(2). The deciding facts rest on artifacts all at weight 1.0: the reason code and timestamps on EV-TRIP-02748, the in-radius dwell and rider presence on EV-GPS-02748, the chat on EV-CHAT-02748 and the fee line on EV-FARE-02748. No POL-NS-08 limb is met (100% coverage, no gaps, chat sequence intact, fare reconciles), so the cap is 1.0. EV-ADVIS-02748-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, but it carries no deciding fact here — the dwell was a single in-geofence interval, so the POL-NS-06(i) accumulation rule that needs a traffic advisory is not in issue — and it is named in the discarded-claim audit below. No POL-NS-09 trigger is engaged (no profile counter in play reaches its test, and no two artifacts contradict each other), so the case is not escalated. The monetary effect is SGD 4.50, which does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so the refund executes automatically on issue. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

How to appeal: Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.
